title: Unscoped enumerator integral conversions
recap: Unscoped enumerations can convert to integral types, while conversion from an arbitrary integer back to an enumeration needs explicit care. Named enumerators need not have consecutive values.
An integer matching the underlying representation is not automatically a recognized domain choice. Validate the accepted codes instead of treating every integer as an enum value.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement permissionValue(permission), returning its integer code, and permissionFromCode(code), accepting exactly codes 0/1/2/4 and returning none/readPermission/writePermission/admin respectively. Unknown codes return none. Do not cast unchecked arbitrary integers into the enum. The enumerators use explicit nonconsecutive values.
hints: Use the explicit values assigned in the enum declaration.
Only three nonzero codes are recognized.
Use none as the fallback, not a cast of the unknown input.
